codes.note: The SUDST is a screening test based on DSM-5, not an interview; its bands are low/moderate/high in Methods and mild/moderate/severe in Table 5. Table 4 is titled 'past 3 months' but uses lifetime-user denominators. Leaf and decoction-mixture users are reported separately and likely overlap; there is no combined kratom figure.

codes.sample: 9 male regular kratom users who drink kratom every day, with no polysubstance use. They were recruited by snowball sampling from one community in Penang, Peninsular Malaysia. Assessments were done at the Advanced Medical and Dental Institute, Universiti Sains Malaysia (ethics code USM/JEPeM/19010054). 15 users were identified and 6 were excluded.
codes.kratom_use_definition: "self-reported as a regular kratom user who consumed kratom on a daily basis in the last 12 months" (brewed kratom juice)
codes.dependence_measures: None. No DSM, ICD, KDS, SDS, ASSIST or diagnostic-interview measure of kratom dependence or use disorder was used. The study assessed only ECG, echocardiogram, serum mitragynine and kratom use history.
codes.possible_duplicate: Same research group (Leong Abdullah, Singh) and Penang community setting as other Malaysian kratom studies, e.g. the Leong Abdullah et al. 2021 ECG study. This report covers only 9 cases.
codes.note: The authors call this a case series of 9 users ("this case series"), so the primary reason for exclusion is E5_design. It would also be excluded under E4_no_dependence_measure, because no kratom dependence or use-disorder measure was used.

codes.sample: Cross-sectional anonymous US national online survey, October 2–26, 2016. Recruited through the American Kratom Association website and social media. 10,000 responses; 8049 completed responses (80.5%) analysed. Adults aged 18+ who currently use kratom.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Current kratom users (self-identified respondents who reported current use of kratom leaf products).
codes.dependence_measures: None for kratom. Measures were demographics, self-rated pain and overall health (5-point Likert/face scale), physician-diagnosed health conditions (including SUD in general, not kratom), and motives for kratom use (illicit or prescription drug dependence, pain, mental/emotional conditions).
codes.possible_duplicate: Same 2016 American Kratom Association online survey dataset (n=8049) as Grundmann 2017 (Drug Alcohol Depend), which reported the first analysis of this survey.
codes.note: No kratom use disorder or dependence instrument was used (no DSM, ICD, KDS, SDS or ASSIST). The only dependence-related items are 'dependence' as a reason for using kratom (self-treating illicit or prescription drug dependence) and a self-reported diagnosed SUD for other substances. Neither of these measures kratom dependence.

codes.sample: Retrospective record review of 2,116 COVID-19 patients at the PSU field hospital, Songkhla, southern Thailand, in 2021. 273 (12.9%) had a first-diagnosed SUD (ICD-10 F10-F19, confirmed by a psychiatrist). Among these 273, 157 (57.5%) used kratom; 94.9% of the 273 were male.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Kratom use was recorded in the psychiatric history of SUD patients who "reported having regularly used substances or alcohol prior to their admission". Median duration of use was 36 months (IQR 12-72); median last use was 1 day before admission. The reference period is current/regular use.
codes.dependence_measures: A psychiatrist made the ICD-10 SUD diagnosis (F10-F19) at interview. The diagnosis was not reported by substance, so there is no kratom-specific use disorder/dependence figure. Kratom withdrawal symptoms were reported (113/157, 72.0%), but withdrawal alone does not count.
codes.possible_duplicate: No other publication from this sample was identified in the text: PSU field hospital, Songkhla, 2021, N=2,116, 273 with SUD, 157 kratom users.
codes.note: Substance use was reviewed only in patients with a first-diagnosed SUD (any substance). All 157 kratom users are in the SUD group, but the F-code may be for another substance (tobacco 82.1%). No kratom-specific count is given. Kratom withdrawal: 113 (72.0%) (Table 2). Reviewer: 157/157 kratom users with any SUD is circular because the sample was selected on SUD.

codes.sample: Students aged 15–19 at one selected upper grammar school (gymnázium) in the Zlín region, Czech Republic. Non-random criterion sample, anonymous online Survio questionnaire, 4–17 Feb 2024. n=258 respondents (144 F, 110 M, 4 other gender). 78 reported lifetime kratom use (p. 37–38).
codes.kratom_use_definition: Lifetime any use ("zkušenost s užíváním kratomu má 78 studentů", p. 37). Last use and usual frequency also reported, e.g. 28 (11 %) used in the past 7 days (p. 41).
codes.dependence_measures: None. The 30-item questionnaire covered sociodemographics, knowledge, prevalence, reasons, dose, form, source, spending, co-use, unpleasant states, health problems, help-seeking and positive effects. No DSM, ICD, KDS, SDS, ASSIST or other dependence or use-disorder measure was applied to kratom.
codes.possible_duplicate: None. Unique single-school sample (Zlín region, Feb 2024, n=258).
codes.note: Czech master's thesis, 2024. Its only mention of dependence is a cited figure from another thesis (p. 23): Medková 2022, a survey of 1,367 Czech kratom users. Quote: "9,9 % respondentů by splňovalo diagnózu syndromu závislosti" ("9.9 % would meet a dependence syndrome diagnosis"). Medková 2022 should be screened separately. The tables are images and are missing here.

codes.sample: Nationwide interviewer-administered household survey of Malaysians aged 15–40 years, January 2020 to July 2021, with random selection of enumeration blocks and living quarters; n=9818. Kratom was not reported as a separate category. It sits inside 'Others' (Table 8: 333 lifetime, 2.8%; 181 current, 1.5%), together with depressants and dissociatives.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Lifetime use and current use (past 30 days). Kratom is grouped with depressants and dissociatives as 'Others' (Table 8 note 8: 'Kratom, depressants, and dissociatives'). The text calls this 'kratom or Mitragyna Speciosa (2.8%)'.
codes.dependence_measures: WHO ASSIST. Current users were sorted into 'mild (0–3), moderate (4–26), and severe (27 and above)' by ASSIST score. These severity bands are reported only for current drug users combined (Table 6), not by substance or for kratom.
codes.possible_duplicate: Nationwide Malaysian youth DSU survey (UKM, funded by KDN/AADK), 2020–2021, n=9818. Other papers from the same survey may report results by substance.
codes.note: ASSIST severity (mild 0.3%, moderate 2.2%, severe 1.0%) is reported only for all current drug users, by age group. There is no figure for kratom users. Kratom use itself is merged into 'Others' with depressants and dissociatives. The bands are labelled mild/moderate/severe, not lower/moderate/high risk. Other papers from this survey may give kratom-specific results.

codes.sample: 129 US adults with lifetime kratom use, recontacted via mTurk Apr 15–May 15, 2021. They came from a larger mTurk substance-use survey unrelated to kratom (Sept 2020–Mar 2021; n=2,615; 289 lifetime kratom users). Mean age 34.8; 51.9% female; 80.6% had ever used >4 times/week; 20.9% had quit.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Lifetime kratom use (any), self-reported at screening into the parent study. Not restricted to current or regular use.
codes.dependence_measures: Lifetime kratom use disorder (KUD), assessed with a DSM-5 SUD checklist modified for kratom (ever qualified, regardless of current use). The cut-off and severity levels are not stated; full results are in Smith et al. 2022 (J Addict Med).

estimates.instrument: Modified DSM-5 SUD checklist for kratom (lifetime)
estimates.threshold_or_category: Qualified for lifetime KUD (cut-off not stated)
estimates.quote: Qualiﬁed for lifetime kratom use disorder 40 31.00

codes.possible_duplicate: Same mTurk kratom recontact survey (US, Apr–May 2021, n=129) as Smith et al. 2022, "Assessment of Kratom Use Disorder and Withdrawal Among an Online Convenience Sample of US Adults" (J Addict Med), which is cited for the full KUD findings. Parent study: Smith et al. 2021a.
codes.note: The only estimate is any lifetime KUD, 40/129 ("Nearly one-third met diagnostic criteria for lifetime KUD"). No severity breakdown or criterion cut-off is given; these are likely in the companion J Addict Med paper. In open-text answers 5/129 (3.9%) mentioned "Addictive/developed dependence", but this is not a standardized measure.

codes.sample: People using several substances (polysubstance users) who were clients of five peer-led, drug-free residential recovery centres in Kentucky, USA. Anonymous survey in April 2017; analysed sample N = 478, of whom 49 (about 10%, reported as 10.4%) reported past-year kratom use. About 85% were referred by the Department of Corrections.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Past-year use: used kratom at least once in the past 12 months.
codes.dependence_measures: None for kratom. The survey asked only about past-year use of substances and the three most preferred drugs. No DSM, ICD, KDS, SDS, ASSIST or other dependence measure was applied to kratom.
codes.possible_duplicate: Same survey as Smith and Lawson 2017: Kentucky residential recovery programs, April 2017, n=503 surveyed (478 analysed). That paper gives the lifetime kratom-use questions and should be checked for any dependence items.
codes.note: Kratom users are reported, but only use prevalence, drug preference (6.25% put kratom among their top three drugs) and regression correlates are given. The text mentions dependence only in the discussion; it was never measured.

codes.sample: 3,382 secondary school students aged 13-19 from 85 schools in NADA-gazetted drug hotspot areas, 8 Malaysian states (Peninsular, Sabah, Sarawak), Dec 2021-Dec 2022, multistage stratified cluster sampling, face-to-face interviews. Kratom users: current 2.8%, lifetime 5.8% (Table 2 'Others' incl. kratom: 68 current, 195 lifetime).
codes.kratom_use_definition: Current use = past 30 days per Methods (Table 2 footnote says within 3 months); lifetime = ever used but not in past 30 days. Kratom is reported inside the ASSIST 'Others' category (kratom, depressant, dissociative).
codes.dependence_measures: ASSIST given; Methods say items covered 'level of risk of drug use or dependency', but no ASSIST scores or risk bands (low/moderate/high) are reported for kratom or any substance.
codes.possible_duplicate: Same LRGS grant (LRGS/1/2019/UKM-UKM/2/1) as Ismail et al. 2022 IJERPH 19:4684 (youths aged 15-40, nationwide), which appears to be a different sample. This study: school adolescents in hotspot areas, 2021-2022, n=3382.
codes.note: Only use prevalence is reported (Table 2; p.5 text 'kratom (2.8%)', 'lifetime use (5.8%)'). Results contain no ASSIST risk or dependence results. no_extractable_counts would also fit, because no risk-band figure is reported for anyone. Inconsistent reference periods: 30 days in Methods vs 3 months in the Table 2 footnote; text gives 2.8% current kratom use vs 2.0% for 'Others' in Table 2.

codes.sample: Czech bachelor's thesis (Charles Univ., 2024). Online survey of adults 18+, recruited Feb–Mar 2024 via kratom Facebook groups plus snowball. 331 responded; 259 lifetime users (79.5% male), 244 past-12-month and 224 past-30-day users. Only the 224 past-30-day users completed the SDS.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Past-30-day use (Q23 "Užil/a jste kratom v průběhu posledních 30 dní?"). This is the subsample (n=224) that completed the SDS. Lifetime use (n=259) defined the wider sample.
codes.dependence_measures: Severity of Dependence Scale (Gossop 1995) for kratom, author's Czech wording; 5 items scored 0–3 (range 0–15). No validated kratom cut-off given. Author cites literature cut-offs (2–4, 4, ≥5) and reports the share scoring ≥6. Full distribution only in Graf 20 (image).

estimates.quote: Přibližně pětina souboru získala nula bodů, celkem 6 a více bodů získalo 28,6 % souboru.

codes.possible_duplicate: No overlap found in the text. Check for a journal article from the same 2024 Czech Facebook survey (n=259 lifetime, 224 past-30-day; supervisor V. Mravčík). Different sample from Medková 2022, Koutenská 2022 and Vostřelová 2021.
codes.note: Czech. "6 a více bodů získalo 28,6 % souboru" = 28.6% scored 6 or more; "pětina…nula bodů" = about a fifth scored 0. The ≥6 cut-off is fixed but not validated for kratom and not called "dependence"; the author says the tool's diagnostic value is limited. ≥4 and ≥5 can't be derived because Graf 20 is missing from the text.

codes.sample: US adults recruited on Amazon mTurk who reported >1 lifetime kratom use in an online substance-use survey (Sep 2020–Mar 2021), recontacted Apr–May 2021. 134 took part; the final analytic sample was 117 (109 for the Quantity task, 114 for the Likelihood task). Mean age 34.7; 50.42% male; 41.9% were current 'regular' users.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Lifetime use: "reported > 1 lifetime use of kratom". Includes current and former regular users.
codes.dependence_measures: Self-report checklist of DSM-5 kratom use disorder (KUD) criteria, for the past year and for lifetime. KUD was defined as "any 2 or more criteria endorsed"; 'mild' KUD = 2–3 symptoms. Severity categories appear only in the supplementary figures.
codes.possible_duplicate: Same mTurk kratom sample as Smith et al., 2022a, 2022b and 2022c (US, survey Sep 2020–Mar 2021, 289 lifetime kratom users identified; recontact subsample n=134/117 in Apr–May 2021). Smith et al. 2022a probably reports KUD prevalence for this sample.
codes.note: The text gives no count or proportion meeting past-year or lifetime KUD, only odds ratios. Counts by KUD status may be in the Fig. 1 legend or in Supplemental Figs 1–2 (past-year KUD categories) and Supplemental Tables 1–2. None of these were provided. Check them; if they have no counts, exclude as no_extractable_counts.

codes.sample: 293 male ketum leaf users surveyed in Penang, Kedah and Perlis (northern Peninsular Malaysia). Cross-sectional design with non-probability (purposive and quota or chain-referral) sampling. All were "medium and long-term" regular users. Community sample, not recruited for kratom problems. 46% were aged 18-25 years.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Regular ketum users, described as medium- and long-term users; the study was "designed to determine severity of ketum dependence in regular ketum users". The exact inclusion criteria (Section 3.7) are not in the text received.
codes.dependence_measures: Leeds Dependence Questionnaire (LDQ), adapted and translated for ketum. The cut-off or scoring used for "severe dependence" (Section 3.11.1) is not in the text received. The study also used the Marijuana Withdrawal Checklist, the MCQ-SF and ASI-5, but these are not dependence measures.

estimates.instrument: Leeds Dependence Questionnaire (LDQ), adapted for ketum
estimates.threshold_or_category: Severe ketum dependence (cut-off not given in the text received)
estimates.location: Abstract, pp. xxii-xxiii (Malay abstract p. xxi)
estimates.quote: A total of 293 ketum users were surveyed ... Fifty-five percent of the sample reported severe ketum dependence

codes.possible_duplicate: Probably the same sample as Singh, Müller & Vicknasingam 2014, Drug Alcohol Depend, "Kratom dependence, withdrawal symptoms and craving in regular users" (n=293; Penang, Kedah, Perlis). This 2013 USM thesis is likely its parent document.
codes.note: The text received stops at p. 24. Missing: Section 3.11.1 (LDQ scoring and cut-off) and the results (4.5.1, Table 4.4 and Figure 4.7, p. 145). Only the abstract figure (55% severe, n=293) is available. If "severe" was defined from the sample's own distribution, the reason would be E3. Pages 116-121 and 144-145 are needed.

codes.sample: 100 regular daily kratom users (all male, mostly Malay; median age 27) and 100 non-using healthy controls. Recruited by snowball sampling from three communities with kratom 'hotspots' in one Malaysian state (USM/AMDI), May 2019–Jan 2020. Analytical cross-sectional lipid-profile study.
codes.kratom_use_definition: "regular and daily kratom use for at least the past 1 year" (inclusion criterion), consumed as kratom juice/tea; mean 3.71 times/day and 4.49 glasses/day.
codes.dependence_measures: No kratom dependence or use-disorder measure was reported. A psychiatrist screened participants with DSM-5 criteria and the MINI only to exclude psychiatric illness, including "substance use and substance-related disorders". No result for kratom users is reported.
codes.possible_duplicate: Likely from the USM (Universiti Sains Malaysia) AMDI kratom research group in northern Peninsular Malaysia, which runs other community studies. Here: 100 male regular kratom users, 2019–2020, recruited by snowball sampling from three community hotspots.
codes.note: Outcomes are lipid profile and liver function only. People with DSM-5/MINI "substance use and substance-related disorders" were excluded. It is unclear whether this covered kratom use disorder, which would make the sample free of it by design. No figure for kratom dependence or use disorder is reported.

codes.sample: Cross-sectional community study (MSc thesis, USM, 2012) in Kedah, Perlis and Penang, northern Peninsular Malaysia. Purposive and chain-referral sampling; 116 men aged 18-65: 41 heroin dependents, 43 active ketum users, 32 non-drug users.
codes.kratom_use_definition: "active ketum users" (abstract). The inclusion criteria (Section 3.4) are not in the text received, so the reference period and frequency are unknown. Short-term and long-term users are compared.
codes.dependence_measures: None seen in the text received. DSM-IV substance dependence criteria appear only as background in the literature review (Table 2.1). It is unknown whether they were applied to ketum users, for example as an inclusion criterion.
codes.possible_duplicate: Centre for Drug Research, USM (Vicknasingam/Mansor group), northern Peninsular Malaysia community ketum samples around 2010-2012. The 43 ketum users may overlap with other CDR USM ketum publications or with a journal article from this thesis.
codes.note: The text stops in Chapter 2 (about p. 24). Missing: methods (3.4 inclusion criteria, 3.6 instruments), results (4.6 ketum use patterns) and appendices. The abstract reports only neurocognitive tests, so E4 is likely. If DSM-IV dependence was an entry criterion, 100% would be dependent by design. Check the full thesis.

codes.sample: Community-based comparison of residents aged 18+ in Nam Phu Subdistrict, Ban Na San District, Surat Thani Province, southern Thailand, an area where the 2017 'Nam Phu Charter' allows traditional kratom use. N=581: 285 kratom users and 296 non-users (Table 1). 78.6% of users were male; their mean age was 55.8.
codes.kratom_use_definition: The text calls participants 'Kratom users' but gives no reference period. Most used kratom 'in their daily life in the traditional way' (chewing fresh leaves). Use characteristics recorded: age at first use, years of use, uses per day, leaves per day, days per week, type of kratom.
codes.dependence_measures: None. The interview covered demographics, health behaviours and kratom use patterns only. Outcomes were fasting serum lipids (total cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL, HDL). No DSM, ICD, KDS, SDS, ASSIST or other dependence measure was used.
codes.possible_duplicate: This may be the same Nam Phu Subdistrict (Surat Thani) community sample used in other papers by La-up, Saengow and Aramrattana (n=581; 285 users). The survey years are not stated.
codes.note: This is a cross-sectional study of how kratom use relates to serum lipid profile. It studied kratom users but did not assess use disorder or dependence. The only outcomes reported are lipid levels and how they relate to kratom use patterns.

codes.sample: Cross-sectional imaging study (MMed dissertation, USM): 12 male kratom users and 13 healthy controls, aged 18–55, at Unit Perubatan Nuklear, IPPT USM (Penang area). Kratom users "were dependent on kratom for more than a year period" and had no illicit drug use (checked by urine toxicology). Study years are not given in the text I received.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Chronic kratom use for more than one year. The abstract says users "were dependent on kratom for more than a year period"; the Malay abstract says "menggunakan ketum untuk tempoh lebih daripada setahun" (used kratom for more than a year).
codes.dependence_measures: Kratom users "were also screened using DSM-V criteria for opioid dependence along with HAM-A, PHQ-9 and MMSE questionnaires" (Abstract, p.14). No cut-off or results for the DSM-5 screen appear in the text I received.
codes.possible_duplicate: This is a thesis, and Chapter 5 is a manuscript prepared for Addiction Biology. A journal article on the same 12 users and 13 controls (IPPT USM) may exist.
codes.note: Text is incomplete: it stops around p.24. Methods 4.3–4.7, the manuscript Results and Appendix 3 (clerking form) are missing. So I can't tell how many of the 12 users met DSM-5 opioid dependence applied to kratom, or whether dependence was an inclusion criterion. If it was, 100% is true by design and the sample may be selected. Please check the full thesis.

codes.sample: Cross-sectional study, convenience sample of 215 adults on Methadone Maintenance Therapy (≥2 months) at the Hospital Taiping methadone clinic, Perak, Malaysia, mid-August to November 2021. 106 (49.3%) were ketum users; 105 of the 106 were male and 88.7% were Malay. They were not recruited because of kratom problems.
codes.kratom_use_definition: The report gives no definition or reference period: "A total of 106 subjects were ketum users". It is unclear whether this means current, past-year or lifetime use.
codes.dependence_measures: KDS (Saingam 2014; Malay version 2018): 16 items, total 0–48; bands 0–13 low, 14–34 moderate, 35–48 high. Given to the 106 ketum users. ASSIST was given to all, with bands low 0–3, moderate 4–26, high 27+, but no kratom-specific score is reported.
codes.possible_duplicate: No overlapping publication known. Sample: Hospital Taiping MMT clinic, Malaysia, Aug–Nov 2021, n=215 (106 ketum users).
codes.note: The only KDS results are Spearman correlations (SOWS–KDS rho=0.570; Table 3); no counts in the KDS bands are reported. Table 2 shows ASSIST high-risk 8 (7.5%) of the 106 ketum users, but this covers any substance, not kratom, so I did not extract it. The KDS band counts might be available from the authors ("available on request").

codes.sample: Cross-sectional community study in Nam Phu sub-district, Ban Na San district, Surat Thani province, Thailand. 581 adults aged 18 or older: 285 kratom users (78.6% male, mean age 55.8) and 296 age-matched non-users. Users were randomly selected from people registered under the Nam Phu Charter. The text does not state the years of data collection.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Past 12 months: "To be regarded as a kratom user, he or she must used kratom within the past 12 months and have registered with the sub-district in accordance with the Nam Phu Charter". The method of use is traditional chewing of fresh leaves.
codes.dependence_measures: None. The study only measured metabolic syndrome (Joint Interim Statement criteria), biochemical values and serum mitragynine. It used no DSM, ICD, KDS, SDS, ASSIST or other dependence or use-disorder measure for kratom.
codes.possible_duplicate: The sample may overlap with other Nam Phu sub-district (Surat Thani) kratom studies by La-up, Saengow, Aramrattana et al., for example the lipid-profile study cited as ref [14]. Site: Nam Phu, Surat Thani; 285 users and 296 non-users.
codes.note: The outcome is metabolic syndrome only. The report gives MetS prevalence for kratom users (11.9%) but nothing on kratom dependence or use disorder, so it fails I3 and I4.

codes.sample: Master's thesis (USM, 2024). 80 adolescents aged 13–19 in compulsory drug rehabilitation (Section 6, Drug Dependants Act 1983), recruited by purposive sampling at 2 PUSPEN centres in Malaysia. Abstract: "60% (n=48/80) had used ketum prior to their detention".
codes.kratom_use_definition: Lifetime kratom use before detention ("pernah menggunakan ketum sebelum ditahan" / "had used ketum prior to their detention"); n=48/80.
codes.dependence_measures: None seen for kratom. The contents list has 3.9.2 "Masalah Penyalahgunaan Bahan (SUD)", content missing. Kratom sections 4.9.x cover motives, duration, quantity, frequency and perception statements (e.g. "can cause addiction", "difficult to stop").
codes.possible_duplicate: Same PUSPEN adolescent sample (n=80, 2 centres, supervisor Darshan Singh) may also appear in journal articles listed under "PENERBITAN" (publications), e.g. on ketum use or HIV risk among adolescent drug users.
codes.note: Text stops at Ch. 1 (section 1.13). Methods, Results and the questionnaire (Lampiran B) are missing, so I can't confirm a kratom dependence measure. The contents list suggests use, motives and perceptions only, so probably E4. Check 3.9.2 and 4.9.x in the full thesis. Malay text; glosses taken from the thesis's English abstract.

codes.sample: Anonymous online self-selected survey of current people who use kratom (PWUK), July 2019–July 2020. Recruited by snowball sampling through social media, kratom online communities, vendors and the American Kratom Association. 7,381 responses; 5,152 valid; 2,296 completed the extended psychiatric module. 96.43% of responses came from the US and Canada.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Current kratom use ("collect responses from current PWUK", p.9). Inclusion criteria: aged over 18 and gave consent.
codes.dependence_measures: None for kratom. The scales used were the ASRS v1.1 (ADHD), PC-PTSD-5 and the SCL-90 depression and anxiety dimensions. Self-reported physician-diagnosed 'Substance use disorder (alcohol, prescription drugs, illicit drugs)' (191, 7.69%, Table 1) is not specific to kratom.
codes.possible_duplicate: Same 2019–2020 University of Florida online survey (IRB #2019-01121) as Grundmann et al. 2022 (AJDAA, motivations) and Grundmann et al. 2022 (Substance Abuse, COVID-19). This text is the Research Square preprint (rs-1923353/v1) of the 2023 article.
codes.note: The sample is people who use kratom, but no kratom use disorder or dependence measure was used. The outcomes are psychiatric screens (ADHD, PTSD, depression, anxiety), co-use of other substances, effects, quality of life and pain. The only SUD item is a self-reported physician diagnosis of any SUD (alcohol, prescription or illicit drugs), not kratom-specific.

codes.sample: This was an anonymous, self-selected online Qualtrics survey of current people who use kratom (PWUK), run July 2019 to July 2020. Recruitment was by snowballing through social media, kratom online communities, vendors and the American Kratom Association. Of 7,381 responses, 5,152 were valid and 2,296 completed the extended psychiatric section. 96.43% were from the US or Canada.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Current kratom use: the survey "was used to collect responses from current PWUK" (p.9). No further reference period or frequency requirement is given.
codes.dependence_measures: None for kratom. Instruments: ASRS v1.1 (ADHD), PC-PTSD-5, SCL-90 depression and anxiety dimensions, EQ-5D-5L, VAS. The only related item is a self-reported diagnosis of "Substance use disorder (alcohol, prescription drugs, illicit drugs)" (191, 7.69%), which is not kratom-specific.
codes.possible_duplicate: Same online survey (July 2019 to July 2020; 5,152 valid responses, mostly US and Canada) as Grundmann, Veltri, Morcos et al. 2022, Am J Drug Alcohol Abuse (self-reported motivations). Probably also related to Grundmann et al. 2022, Substance Abuse (COVID-19).
codes.note: Research Square preprint (2022). Screens people who use kratom for ADHD, PTSD, depression and anxiety only. Kratom use disorder or dependence is not assessed (no DSM, ICD, KDS, SDS or ASSIST). The self-reported SUD diagnosis (Table 1) is not kratom-specific. The survey instrument is in supplementary material that was not provided, but the text mentions no dependence measure.

codes.sample: 12,007 incarcerated adults entering the Kentucky Department of Corrections Substance Abuse Treatment Program (SAP), surveyed 2016–2018 (Kentucky residents for more than 6 months of the pre-incarceration year). Of these, 3,142 (26.2%) reported diverted buprenorphine use. Very few reported kratom use (0.19% vs 0.07% by buprenorphine group), and no kratom-user subsample is analysed.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Use in the 12 months before incarceration, from dichotomised answers on the number of months of use. Reported only as percentages within the buprenorphine and non-buprenorphine groups.
codes.dependence_measures: DSM-5-based survey items for moderate/severe SUD in the year before incarceration, for ANY drug, not kratom-specific: "participants were not asked to specify a drug for SUD assessment, as the survey was designed to only assess the presence of any SUD." Survey items were adapted from the ASI-5.
codes.possible_duplicate: Kentucky DOC SAP baseline assessment data, 2016–2018 (N=12,007). Other papers from the same evaluation dataset may exist (e.g., Smith et al., 2019, cited in the text).
codes.note: Kratom appears only as one past-year use variable (Results: "kratom (0.19 % vs. 0.07 %, p < .001)"; AOR = 1.90, p = .172). The SUD assessment was DSM-5 based but not drug-specific: there is no kratom use disorder or dependence measure and no SUD figure for kratom users. E4 is assigned as the first reason that applies; E2 would also apply.

codes.sample: 50 men from Bannasarn district (Surat Thani) and Natawee district (Songkhla), southern Thailand: 31 long-term kratom chewers (LKC) and 19 matched controls who did not use kratom. LKC used kratom for a mean of 18.13 ± 11.04 years and chewed a mean of 11.65 ± 10.12 leaves/day.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Current daily use of at least 2 years: "daily kratom chewing (2 years)" of fresh kratom leaves; the last chew had to be at least 2 h before testing.
codes.dependence_measures: None for kratom. The only instruments named are the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (used for exclusion) and questionnaires on demographics and kratom use history (duration, leaves/day). Outcomes were heart rate variability indices (LFn, HFn).
codes.possible_duplicate: The sample may overlap with Saengmolee et al., 2022 (EEG study of long-term kratom chewers in southern Thailand, same research group). This report: Surat Thani/Songkhla, 31 male LKC, ethics approval HSc-HREC-63-017-1-1.
codes.note: This is a case-control study of cardiac autonomic function (HRV) in long-term kratom chewers. No kratom use disorder or dependence assessment (DSM, ICD, KDS, SDS, ASSIST, etc.) is reported. Kratom users were studied, but only use duration and quantity were measured, so the primary reason is E4.

codes.sample: US 2019 National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH), n=56,136, civilian non-institutionalized population aged 12+. Lifetime kratom users made up 1.5% of the weighted sample; their unweighted n is not reported.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Self-reported lifetime kratom use. Of these users, 50.9% last used more than a year ago, 28.4% within the past year and 20.7% within the past month.
codes.dependence_measures: Past-year substance use disorders (SUDs) as assessed in NSDUH for opioids, stimulants, methamphetamine, cocaine, alcohol, marijuana, tranquilizers/sedatives and others. Kratom use disorder was not assessed. The report does not name the criteria version.
codes.possible_duplicate: NSDUH 2019 kratom data are used in several other papers. Sample: US national household survey, 2019, n=56,136.
codes.note: SUDs among kratom users are reported only for other substances: "31% ... of kratom users had at least one SUD" and opioid use disorder at 8.9%. No kratom use disorder figure is given. E4 could also apply, since no kratom-specific measure was used. I chose E2 because SUDs were measured but reported only for other substances.

codes.sample: US adults recruited nationwide July-Oct 2022 (Reddit, Facebook, American Kratom Association, etc.) for a 15-day smartphone EMA study (NIDA IRP). 395 enrolled; 357 completed the EMA and make up the analytic sample. Mean age 38.0 years, 55.5% men, 91.0% White, 37.8% currently in alcohol or drug recovery. Participants were grouped into 5 use-pattern clusters (A-E).
codes.kratom_use_definition: Current regular use: inclusion required "kratom use (≥3 times weekly for ≥4 weeks)". Most participants used daily, mainly whole-leaf products.
codes.dependence_measures: Baseline survey item set on past-year DSM-5-based criteria for substance use disorder applied to kratom (KUD), self-report. Case definition: KUD = ≥2 symptoms. Severity categories (mild/moderate/severe) are not reported in the text; symptom counts are shown only in Figure 4A.

codes.possible_duplicate: Same NIDA nationwide EMA sample (US, July-Oct 2022, 395 enrolled / 357 completers) as the separately published methods paper (ref 13), the interview substudy of EMA participants (ref 23), and any later papers using lab assays of the same participants' products.
codes.note: Cluster n's come only from the denominators for men: 56, 65, 71, 83, 80 (sum 355, not 357). The D and E percentages fit n=84 and n=81 instead; check eTable 2. Three participants met KUD criteria through tolerance and withdrawal only. No mild/moderate/severe breakdown is in the text; it may be in Figure 4A or the supplement, which were not available.

codes.sample: This is the 2008 Thai National Mental Health Survey, a household survey of people aged 15–59 years in all five regions of Thailand (N=17,140). Of these, 537 had used illicit drugs in the past year, and 317 of them (59%) had used kratom.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Use in the past 12 months. Respondents were asked about each drug, including "kratom leaves (Mitragyna speciosa Korth)", during the year before the interview ("current illicit drug users"). Use was recorded only as yes or no.
codes.dependence_measures: None for kratom or other drugs. The MINI 5.0 (Thai) was used only for mental disorders, alcohol abuse/dependence and suicidality. The paper says "an instrument for the diagnosis of SUDs did not apply in the 2008 Thai NMH Survey... abuse or dependent patterns were not assessed" (p. 457).
codes.possible_duplicate: Same sample as the 2008 Thai NMH Survey (N=17,140, June–August 2008) used in Suttajit et al. 2012 (Addict Behav 37:1395), Srisurapanont et al. 2012 (Addict Behav 37:173) and Junsirimongkol et al. 2011 (J Ment Health Thai).
codes.note: There is a kratom-user subsample (n=317, p. 455), but no drug or kratom use disorder or dependence was assessed. Only alcohol use disorders were measured with the MINI. The 162 illicit drug users with alcohol use disorders are not a kratom-specific figure and do not measure kratom dependence.

codes.sample: Cross-sectional anonymous online convenience survey (Qualtrics) of American Kratom Association and Global Kratom Coalition members, USA, March–September 2025. Adults ≥18 with past or current kratom use; n=161 included (154 current, 7 previous users).
codes.kratom_use_definition: Lifetime any use: "adults 18 years and older who reported kratom use currently or at any point in the past"; 95.7% current use.
codes.dependence_measures: No kratom dependence or use-disorder instrument was used. The novel questionnaire asked about reported medical diagnoses, including "SUD/dependence" (29/135; diagnosed by an HCP or self-diagnosed). These SUDs were for other substances (alcohol, opioids, tobacco, etc.), not kratom.
codes.note: Study covers when kratom was started relative to other substances and medical care, plus reasons for use. The only SUD figure is self-reported SUD "related to alcohol (62.1%), opioids (51.7%), tobacco (31.1%)...", not kratom. The questionnaire appendix was not provided, but the methods describe no kratom dependence items.

codes.sample: Doctoral thesis (Maastricht/Sapienza, 2025). Ch.2 systematic review; Ch.3 literature review; Ch.4 YouTube netnography; Ch.5 darknet product inventory; Ch.6 phase 1 mitragynine trial in healthy volunteers; Ch.7 use patterns of classic/novel/herbal opioids (qualitative online research per outline). No primary sample of kratom users with a dependence measure in received text.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Not applicable; no primary sample of kratom users assessed for dependence in the received text.
codes.dependence_measures: None applied to a primary sample. Ch.2 Table 2 only cites other studies (e.g., Singh et al. 2014 LDQ; Leong Bin Abdullah 2019a KDS), i.e., secondary review data.
codes.possible_duplicate: Ch.2 published as Prevete et al. 2022 Hum Psychopharmacol (review); Ch.3 as Prevete et al. 2023 Curr Addict Rep (review). Other chapters likely published separately.
codes.note: Text truncated at 400,000 chars (ends early in Ch.3); Ch.4-8 not seen. Outline (p.17-18) says Ch.4/5/7 are qualitative online research and Ch.6 is a healthy-volunteer phase 1 trial. Reviewer should check Ch.7 in full thesis: if it is a survey of kratom users with a dependence measure (e.g., DSM-5/SDS), reclassify.

codes.sample: 102 ethnobotanical tea bar patrons aged 18–51 (mean age 22.34, 39.2% women), recruited by street-intercept field surveys at two tea bars in Northern Colorado, USA, fall 2023 to spring 2024. Those without past-year kratom use (N = 4) were excluded from analysis, so the analysed sample is about 98.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Past-year kratom use. "Individuals who did not report past-year kratom use (N = 4) were excluded from analysis" (p. 2).
codes.dependence_measures: None. Measures were only open-ended items on adverse reactions (dose, contextual factors, duration, harm reduction strategies) and a yes/no item on seeking medical attention. DSM-5 is mentioned only in the Introduction, when discussing the literature.
codes.possible_duplicate: Same pilot sample as Piercey CJ et al., "Kratom use among ethnobotanical tea bar patrons in Colorado", Drug Alcohol Depend Rep 2025;16:100361 (ref 38): Northern Colorado tea bars, 2023–2024, n = 102. Check that paper separately for any dependence or use-disorder measure.
codes.note: Brief report giving descriptive percentages and thematic analysis of acute adverse reactions and harm reduction strategies. It reports no kratom use disorder or dependence instrument and no estimate of it. Use patterns are said to be in ref 38.

codes.sample: No empirical sample. This is a narrative review of proteomic and analytical methods (urinary biomarkers, LC-MS/MS, IMS, ELISA) for detecting kratom use and addiction. It is labelled "Research Article" but includes no methods, participants or results.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Not applicable. No kratom users were sampled.
codes.dependence_measures: None. No DSM, ICD, KDS, SDS, ASSIST or other dependence instrument was applied. The text discusses only the idea of urinary protein biomarkers for "diagnosis of kratom addiction".
codes.possible_duplicate: None.
codes.note: Literature overview (Jasim, Basheer, Gam 2022, Universiti Sains Malaysia). Conclusion p.4 (p.177): "Proteomics approach may be used to investigate a useful biomarker, preferably from urine for diagnosis of kratom addiction." No prevalence data. The running headers on pp.2-7 wrongly cite a different article (Shedge et al. 2021, Paclitaxel-Copper); this looks like a PDF artefact.

codes.sample: Cross-sectional community survey in April 2023, using purposive selection of communities with high kratom use in southern Thailand (Prince of Songkla University community medicine project). N=169 adults; 45 current kratom users (26.6%), 23 former, 101 never. Current users were 86.7% male, mean age 41.8 years.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Self-reported current kratom use (n=45); no reference period stated. Former users (n=23) are also mentioned, but the usage-pattern tables cover only current users.
codes.dependence_measures: None validated. The outcome "harmful use" is a dose cut-off: >20 leaves/day (~>150 mg mitragynine/day). There are single ad hoc items on craving and increased use. No DSM, ICD, KDS, SDS, ASSIST or diagnostic interview was used.
codes.possible_duplicate: Not obviously a duplicate. Sample: southern Thai high-prevalence communities (mostly Muslim, fishing), April 2023, N=169 (45 current users). Communities and province are not named.
codes.note: The only case definition is dose-based "harmful use": 22/45 (48.9%) used >20 leaves/day (p.1, Table 2). This is a quantity threshold, not a dependence instrument. Table 2 also has ad hoc items "Craving to use 9 (20.0)" and "Perceptions of increased consumption 9 (20.0)", which are not a scale with a cut-off. Supplementary S1 (the questionnaire) was not provided; the reviewer may want to check it.

codes.sample: US nationwide remote sample of adults who use kratom regularly. Recruited online and through kratom stakeholders and social media, 20 July–18 October 2022. 395 people consented, enrolled and completed the survey; 388 took part in the 15-day EMA phase.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Regular use: "use ≥3 times weekly for ≥4 weeks prior to screening" (current regular use).
codes.dependence_measures: Kratom use disorder was assessed with "generic criteria for substance use disorders from the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual, fifth revision" (Smith et al., 2022c). Physical dependence symptoms were also asked about. No cut-offs or results are reported.
codes.possible_duplicate: NIDA IRP remote EMA and product-assay study of US adults who use kratom regularly (July–October 2022; n=395 enrolled, n=388 in EMA). Kratom use disorder results for this cohort are probably reported in other papers by Smith et al.; check those.
codes.note: Methods and feasibility paper. It says "We evaluated kratom use disorder and symptoms of physical dependence" but gives no count or proportion meeting KUD or dependence criteria; only enrollment, compliance and shipment figures. The supplementary material is described as the product form and instructions. A companion paper on this sample may be eligible.

codes.sample: The protocol mentions only "regular kratom users and healthy non-kratom using subjects" who had blood drawn at AMDI, Universiti Sains Malaysia. It gives no sample size, site details, recruitment details or results.
codes.kratom_use_definition: "Regular kratom users". This protocol does not define the term (no frequency or duration of use is given).
codes.dependence_measures: None in this text. The protocol covers only laboratory steps: fasting lipid profile and liver function tests run on a Beckman Coulter AU680.
codes.possible_duplicate: Companion protocol to Leong Bin Abdullah MFI et al. 2020, PLoS ONE 15(6):e0234639 (regular kratom users vs non-users, USM Malaysia). Screen that article separately; its sample may overlap with other USM/Singh community studies.
codes.note: This is a lab-methods protocol with no results. It describes blood collection and how lipid and liver tests were run. It has no participant counts and no assessment of kratom dependence or use disorder, so it is excluded as a protocol without results (E5). E4 would also apply. The linked PLoS ONE article may contain dependence data and should be retrieved and screened separately.

codes.sample: 151 ex-opioid users on methadone maintenance therapy (≥12 months, with chronic pain symptoms ≥6 months) at 2 MMT clinics in Alor Setar, Kedah, Malaysia (KKBAS n=104, HSB n=47), July–September 2016; 97.4% male, 91.4% Malay. Subsample of regular kratom users: 61 (40.4%).
codes.kratom_use_definition: Regular use of kratom, defined as "Use of any kratom products daily" (Table 1 footnote c). Current daily use; no explicit reference period given.
codes.dependence_measures: None for kratom. The instruments used were BPI (pain), BFI neuroticism, BDI and BAI. Kratom was recorded only as a yes/no regular-use variable.
codes.note: The report gives only the prevalence of daily kratom use (61/151, 40.4%; Table 1, p.2) and how it relates to chronic severe pain (crude OR 2.648, Table 2). No kratom dependence or use-disorder measure (DSM, ICD, KDS, SDS, ASSIST or a diagnostic interview) was used. The authors call for further studies on "the impact and the severity of kratom use" (pp.3-4).

codes.sample: 293 regular kratom users (all male, all Malay, mean age 28) from 15 communities in Penang, Perlis and Kedah, Malaysia. Snowball sampling, Jan–Dec 2012. Adults with at least 6 months of use. Excluded people in drug treatment or with a positive urine test for illicit drugs.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Current regular kratom use with self-reported use for at least 6 months ("self-reported kratom use of at least six months"). All drank processed kratom juice.
codes.dependence_measures: Only the ASI 5th edition (past 30 days), used for social functioning, with no cut-off or dependence case definition. Dependence appears only as one self-report item: "Almost 99% claimed kratom was among one of the major substances that they were dependent on".
codes.possible_duplicate: Probably the same sample as Singh, Müller & Vicknasingam 2014, Drug Alcohol Depend 139:132-137 (northern Peninsular Malaysia, 2012, n=293 regular users). That paper reportedly used the SDS and may be the eligible source.
codes.note: The ASI covered social functioning domains only. No validated dependence or use-disorder instrument with a cut-off was applied to kratom. The 99% figure (p.127) is a single unvalidated self-report item. "Kratom can cause dependence: Yes 83%" (Table 1) is a belief item. The reviewer may decide whether the 99% item counts; as written it does not meet I3.

codes.sample: Online anonymous cross-sectional survey on Qualtrics, Feb 10 to May 11, 2023. Nonprobability sample of adults (18+) who currently consume kratom, recruited via the American Kratom Association listserv, pro- and anti-kratom Facebook groups and downstream social media. 2824 responses; analysed N=2061 (52.3% male, mean age 47.8). Mostly US, 6.8% outside the US.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Current kratom consumption, checked by a screening question ("ensure participants reported current kratom consumption"). The 253 respondents not actively using kratom were screened out.
codes.dependence_measures: The 11 DSM-5 SUD criteria adapted for kratom, self-reported in the survey. KUD = 2 or more criteria; mild = 2-3, moderate = 4-5, severe = 6 or more. The criteria time frame (e.g. past year) is not stated.

codes.sample: 250 support staff (central supply, laundry, nutrition, central transport/vehicle units) at one tertiary hospital in Bangkok, Thailand, interviewed in 2024 (B.E. 2567). Convenience sample, cross-sectional. Kratom subsamples: 80 lifetime kratom-leaf users (32.0%) and 65 lifetime kratom-cocktail users (26.0%). Past 3 months: 9 leaf users and 14 cocktail users.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Lifetime use (ASSIST Q1) of kratom leaves (ใบกระท่อม) and, separately, of the kratom boiled-leaf mixture/cocktail (สารผสมน้ำต้มใบกระท่อม: 4x100, 8x100, etc.). ASSIST risk bands are reported with lifetime users as the denominator.
codes.dependence_measures: WHO ASSIST V3.1, Thai version (Assanangkornchai et al. 2011), given by interview. Substance-specific involvement score is the sum of Q2–Q7. Bands for substances other than alcohol: 0–3 low, 4–26 moderate, ≥27 high risk ("likely dependent").
codes.possible_duplicate: The text received is the Chula master's thesis (Kanchanasim, ETD 74605, 2024). The record is a 2026 J Med Bioscience article with the same title, so both likely describe one sample: 250 support staff, one Bangkok tertiary hospital, 2024. Count once.
codes.note: Thai text. Glosses: ใบกระท่อม = kratom leaves; น้ำต้มใบกระท่อม = boiled-leaf mixture (4x100 cocktail); เสี่ยงต่ำ/กลาง/สูง = low/moderate/high risk. Leaf and cocktail users are reported separately, probably overlap, with no combined kratom figure. The leaf high-risk cell is printed "-" (presumably 0). The bands cover the past 3 months, but the denominators are lifetime users.

codes.sample: 150 regular kratom users, all male, mean age 34.4 years, almost all Malay (99%). Recruited by snowball and purposive sampling over 1 year at three community locations in Penang, Malaysia. Exclusions: positive urine test for other drugs, alcohol or illicit drug use in the past year, past or present psychiatric or medical illness. Not recruited because of kratom problems.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Current regular use: self-reported regular kratom user who "used kratom ≥2 times daily", with more than 1 year of kratom use history. All respondents used kratom daily.
codes.dependence_measures: Kratom Dependence Scale (KDS), Malay version: 16 items scored 0-3, total 0-48. Bands: 0-13 mild, 14-34 moderate, 35-48 severe dependence. For the analysis the bands were grouped as KDS <35 (mild and moderately severe) and KDS ≥35 (severe).

codes.sample: 293 male regular kratom users recruited by purposive sampling in community settings in Penang, Perlis and Kedah, northern peninsular Malaysia, Jan–Dec 2012. People who tested urine-positive for other drugs were excluded, as were those who had used kratom for less than 6 months. Mean age 28.9; 36.5% were ex-drug users. Not recruited because of kratom problems.
codes.kratom_use_definition: Regular use: current kratom use (boiled leaf juice) for >6 months ("those who drank Kratom several times per day for more than 6 month"). Mean 3.5 glasses per day.
codes.dependence_measures: Leeds Dependence Questionnaire (LDQ; Raistrick et al., 1994), applied to kratom, Malay translation. Moderate and severe categories are reported; the cut-off scores are not stated. Withdrawal (MWC) and craving (MCQ-SF) were also measured.

estimates.quote: More than half of the respondents (161/293) faced severe Kratom dependence problems
while 45% (132/293) had moderate Kratom dependence problems

codes.possible_duplicate: Probably the same 2012 community sample (Penang/Perlis/Kedah, n=293 male regular users) used in other papers by Singh, Vicknasingam, Müller et al. Check for overlap.
codes.note: All 293 users fell into the moderate or severe LDQ categories ("All others had moderate..."). There was no none/mild category and the LDQ cut-offs are not reported. Withdrawal and craving figures are not dependence measures. The comparison by duration of use is reported only as 'not significant', with no counts. Purposive sample of men only.

codes.sample: Cross-sectional house-to-house survey of adults aged 18 and over at FELDA Chuping, Perlis, Malaysia, July–October 2017 (randomised houses, convenience recruitment). N=144, of whom 35 (24.3%) were kratom users (33 male, 2 female).

codes.dependence_measures: ASSIST-Malay version with kratom in item J. Only a mean specific substance involvement score is reported for kratom (11.46, SD 10.918), with no risk bands. MINI (DSM-IV) Module J, Substance Dependence/Abuse, which is not stated to be specific to kratom.
